subject: Quality delta seen in quantized A/B — triage, acceptance criteria, and roadmap asks
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quality delta seen in quantized A/B — triage, acceptance criteria, and roadmap asks

Team,

Quick heads-up from the overnight A/B run we kicked off against the new int8-like quantization profile (q4r) on the staging canary: the overall token throughput improvement looks good, but we're seeing a measurable quality delta on a subset of prompts in our Nimbus Health promptset (attached summary). High-level: a ~3.8% increase in hallucination-style false-assertions on the patient-summary prompts and a 1.7 pt drop on the clinical-entity F1 compared to baseline.

I attached a csv with the delta breakdown and a small sample of the failing prompts (promptset_v14_examples.txt). No customer-facing alerts yet, but Nimbus is running extended smoke tests today and we should act quickly.

Asks:
- Can infra confirm whether the q4r runtime path touched cache/KV indexing or prompt normalization? (Dev)
- Can Applied ML own a focused rerun against the 1,000-sample stratified shard (neha)? We need a tight confidence interval on the delta and a root-cause hypothesis. (Marissa / Neha)
- Product: do we want to pause the canary rollout for q4r while we triage? If so, I'll request a temporary canary-hold from Release. Also need clear acceptance criteria to re-enable. (Karthik)

Suggested acceptance criteria (draft):
- Hallucination-rate uplift <= 1.0% relative to baseline on the critical patient-summary prompt group
- Clinical-entity F1 no more than 0.5 points below baseline
- No reproducible regression on the top-10 high-sensitivity prompts used in Nimbus smoke tests

Timeline: aim to have initial reproduce + hypothesis by EOD (PST). If we need an exception to the auto-rollback policy, call it out explicitly and include the impact analysis.

Attachments: 2027-03-10-quality-delta-summary.csv, promptset_v14_examples.txt

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quality delta seen in quantized A/B — triage, acceptance criteria, and roadmap asks

Thanks Alex — I pulled the csv.

Neha: can you take point on the reproduce and narrow down whether this is data-distribution-sensitive (longer clinical notes) vs model-side tokenization/quantization sensitivity? I'll run a parallel small prompt ablation on my end to identify the most fragile templates.

A couple of concrete metric proposals to consider as acceptance criteria (to supplement Alex's):
- A/B test with bootstrapped CI, 95% CI overlapping baseline for both hallucination and F1 metrics
- If a metric crosses threshold, require an explanation-level repro (sample-by-sample trace) before any rollback exception is approved

I'll add promptset_v14_examples.txt to our eval harness and tag the failing samples.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Applied ML — Evaluations
Redwood Inference

Adding some infra context — I pushed a short notes patch and a hotfix branch that addresses a KV-cache alignment mismatch we discovered while instrumenting q4r. The branch (link below) includes an optional fallthrough path we can enable for the canary that preserves pre-q4r tokenization for sensitive prompt groups.

Repo: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/runtime/compare/qint-fix
Branch: hotfix/kv-alignment-q4r
Patch: hotfix_branch-notes.patch (attached)

Immediate plan: we can create a canary variant that uses the hotfix path for requests with the Nimbus promptset tag and leave the rest of the canary on q4r. That should let Nimbus continue tests without global rollback. Need product sign-off (Karthik) and a short smoke confirmation from Applied ML.

Also: please provide a test harness endpoint (staging) with the promptset shard so we can reproduce at scale — Ops can provision.

—Dev
Dev Patel

Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Plan: focused A/B + temporary canary pause request

Thanks all for the quick replies — summary and next steps: 

1) Reproduce (Neha & Marissa): run the stratified 1k-sample A/B against baseline vs q4r + hotfix path. Please include per-sample trace and the prompt tags so we can identify cluster patterns. Target: complete by EOD PST.

2) Infra (Dev): stand up a staging endpoint with the promptset shard and enable the hotfix branch as a canary variant targeted at Nimbus prompts. Send the staging URL when ready.

3) Product (Karthik): I will formally request a temporary canary pause for global q4r rollout until the narrow A/B completes. If Product approves, Release will stop the expansion and we keep the hotfix-targeted canary for Nimbus.

4) Acceptance criteria (draft, final to be agreed):
   - Hallucination-rate uplift <= 1.0% absolute vs baseline on patient-summary group
   - Clinical-entity F1 drop <= 0.5 pts vs baseline
   - No reproducible failure across top-10 Nimbus smoke prompts
   - Per-sample trace present for any failing case

5) Communication: I'll ping customer contacts (Ellen @ Nimbus) if we pause the global rollout; we should phrase it as a targeted additional validation step and offer the hotfix canary so their tests can continue.

Attachments: promptset_v14_examples.txt

If anyone disagrees with the plan or the acceptance thresholds, call it out now — otherwise I'll open the RD ticket and request the pause.

Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan: focused A/B + temporary canary pause request

Agree with the plan and thresholds.

Two asks from Product side:
- Approve the temporary global-canary pause. Please include a short customer note for Ellen (Nimbus) — I'll review before send.
- Add a monitoring hook in Redwood Console for the hallucination signal (per-route) and tie the evaluation alert to RD-1428 so this gets prioritized on the roadmap for the next sprint.

I'll mark this P1 for release-scheduler and approve the targeted hotfix-canary approach. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
